sections.title: Executive Summary + Investment Thesis
sections.body:
Executive Summary:
ITC Limited has undergone a significant development with the demerger of its Hotels Business into ITC Hotels Limited (ITCHL) effective January 1, 2025. ITCHL, with 39.88% shareholding held by ITC Limited, operates a diverse portfolio of 140+ properties and over 13,000 rooms across six distinctive brands. The company's financial reporting is guided by Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS) and reflects a comprehensive approach to consolidation, revenue recognition, and financial instrument accounting. 

Investment Thesis:
Our investment thesis is centered on ITC Limited's diversified business portfolio and its strategic move to demerge the Hotels Business into ITCHL. With ITCHL poised as one of the fastest-growing hospitality chains in the country, we anticipate potential for growth in the hospitality segment. However, without specific financial data such as revenue from operations or net profit, it is challenging to provide a detailed financial outlook. Further analysis of ITC Limited's consolidated financial statements and industry trends would be necessary to fully assess the investment potential of the company.

sections.title: Business Overview + Segment Breakdown
sections.body:
ITC's corporate strategy focuses on creating multiple drivers of growth anchored on its core competencies, with a current emphasis on three business groups: FMCG, Paperboards, Paper & Packaging, and Agri Business. The company's organisational structure and governance processes are designed to support effective management of multiple businesses while retaining focus on each one. The Operating Segments have been reported in a manner consistent with the internal reporting provided to the Corporate Management Committee, which is the Chief Operating Decision Maker.

The business groups comprise the following segments: FMCG (Cigarettes and Others, including Branded Packaged Foods Businesses, Education and Stationery Products, Personal Care Products, Safety Matches, and Agarbattis), Paperboards, Paper and Packaging, Agri Business (Agri commodities such as wheat, rice, spices, coffee, soya, and leaf tobacco), and Others (including ITC Grand Central Hotel, Mumbai). The segment results of ‘FMCG : Others’ are after considering significant business development, brand building, and gestation costs of the Branded Packaged Foods businesses and Personal Care Products business. As of 2025, the company's revenue from external customers within India was ₹65,635.22 crore, while revenue from external customers outside India is not fully disclosed. The company's capital expenditure and depreciation and amortization for each segment are also reported, with FMCG - Cigarettes having a capital expenditure of ₹320.52 crore and depreciation and amortization of ₹266.20 crore in 2025.

sections.title: Management Commentary
sections.body:
The management of ITC has outlined a corporate strategy focused on creating multiple drivers of growth, anchored on its core competencies, across three primary business groups: FMCG, Paperboards, Paper & Packaging, and Agri Business. As of the latest reporting period, the company's organisational structure and governance processes are designed to support effective management of these multiple businesses. The Operating Segments have been reported in a manner consistent with the internal reporting provided to the Corporate Management Committee, which is the Chief Operating Decision Maker. Notably, the Hotels Business (excluding ITC Grand Central, Mumbai) has been reported as 'Discontinued Operations' pursuant to the Scheme of Demerger, with the results of ITC Grand Central, Mumbai disclosed under a new 'Others' segment.

The company's management has also provided insight into the geographical information, with revenue from external customers reported as ₹65,635.22 crore within India and an undisclosed amount outside India for the year 2025. Furthermore, the management has highlighted that segment results of 'FMCG: Others' are after considering significant business development, brand building, and gestation costs of the Branded Packaged Foods businesses and Personal Care Products business. The company's capital expenditure and depreciation and amortization expenses have been disclosed, with ₹1,327.65 crore and ₹1,313.83 crore, respectively, for the year 2025. However, specific details on net profit (PAT) and net worth (shareholders' equity) are not provided in the given excerpts.

sections.title: Recent Developments
sections.body:
Recent Developments: 
The company has reported its Hotels Business (excluding ITC Grand Central, Mumbai) as 'Discontinued Operations' pursuant to the Scheme of Demerger and applicable Accounting Standards (Ind AS). As a result, 'Hotels' no longer forms a reportable segment of the company, with the exception of ITC Grand Central, Mumbai, which has been retained and disclosed under a new 'Others' segment. In the year under review, ITC Infotech India Limited, a subsidiary of the company, recorded revenue from operations of ₹3204.32 crores and a net profit of ₹466.62 crores. The company paid a total dividend of ₹53.75 per equity share, aggregating ₹488.32 crores. Additionally, ITC Infotech India Limited has set up subsidiary companies in several countries, including Brazil, Mexico, France, Germany, Italy, Malaysia, and Saudi Arabia, as part of its expansion efforts.

In terms of capital expenditure, the company incurred ₹1842.28 crores in the current year, with the FMCG segment accounting for ₹836.32 crores, Agri Business for ₹104.07 crores, and Paperboards, Paper and Packaging for ₹381.84 crores. The company's revenue from external customers within India was ₹65,635.22 crores, while revenue from outside India is not explicitly stated in the provided excerpts. Overall, the company's recent developments reflect its focus on diversifying its business segments and expanding its global presence through its subsidiaries.

sections.title: Bull vs Bear vs Base Case
sections.body:
The bull case for ITC is supported by the company's diversified business portfolio, which includes FMCG, Paperboards, Paper & Packaging, and Agri Business. The company's revenue from operations within India has shown an increase, with ₹65,635.22 crores in 2025 compared to ₹60,333.03 crores in 2024. Additionally, the company's profit after tax from discontinued operations stood at ₹15,103.76 crores in 2025, including an exceptional gain on demerger of ₹15,163.06 crores. This demonstrates the company's ability to generate significant profits from its divested businesses.

On the other hand, the bear case for ITC highlights the company's dependence on its FMCG segment, which accounted for a significant portion of its revenue. The segment results of 'FMCG: Others' are after considering significant business development, brand building, and gestation costs, which may impact profitability. Furthermore, the company's capital expenditure and depreciation costs have increased, with total capital expenditure standing at ₹18,422.28 crores in 2025 compared to ₹16,688.88 crores in 2024. The base case scenario assumes that ITC will continue to diversify its business portfolio and generate steady revenue growth, driven by its core competencies in FMCG, Paperboards, Paper & Packaging, and Agri Business. However, the exact revenue and net profit growth rates are not specified in the provided context, and therefore, cannot be determined.

Principles of Consolidation The Group’s interests in its subsidiaries, associates and joint ventures are reflected in the Consolidated Financial Statements (CFS) in accordance with the relevant Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS) specified under Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013. Subsidiaries (Ind AS 110) Line by line consolidation of the Statement of Profit and Loss and Balance Sheet is done by aggregating like items of assets, liabilities, income and expenses. The excess / deficit of the cost to ITC Limited of its investments in its subsidiaries over its share of net worth (residual interest in the assets of the subsidiaries after deducting all its liabilities) of the subsidiaries at the date of investment in the subsidiaries are treated as goodwill / capital reserve in the CFS. The goodwill is disclosed as an asset and capital reserve as a reserve in the Consolidated Balance Sheet. Profit or loss and each component of other comprehensive income are attributed to the Group as owners and to the non-controlling interest; likewise the non-controlling interests in the net assets of the consolidated subsidiaries is identified and presented separately within Equity in the Consolidated Balance Sheet. Inter-Company transactions within the Group (both Balance Sheet and Profit or loss items) are eliminated for arriving at the Group CFS. CFS is prepared applying uniform accounting policies of ITC Limited to the Group companies. Associates and Joint Ventures (Ind AS 28) An investment in associate and joint venture is initially recognised at cost on the date of the investment, and is inclusive of any goodwill / capital reserve embedded in the cost. Only share of net profits / losses and other comprehensive income of associates / joint ventures is considered in Consolidated Statement of Profit and Loss. The carrying amount of the investment in associates / joint ventures is adjusted by the share of net profits / losses and other comprehensive income in the Consolidated Balance Sheet. 224 REPORT AND ACCOUNTS 2025 ITC Limited

Financial Liabilities Borrowings, trade payables and other financial liabilities are initially recognised at fair value and are subsequently measured at amortised cost. Any discount or premium on redemption / settlement is recognised in the Statement of Profit and Loss as finance cost over the life of the liability using the effective interest method and adjusted to the liability figure disclosed in the Balance Sheet. Financial liabilities are derecognised when the liability is extinguished, that is, when the contractual obligation is discharged, cancelled or on expiry. Offsetting Financial Instruments Financial assets and liabilities are offset and the net amount is included in the Balance Sheet where there is a legally enforceable right to offset the recognised amounts and there is an intention to settle on a net basis or realise the asset and settle the liability simultaneously. Equity Instruments Equity instruments are recognised at the value of the proceeds, net of direct costs of the capital issue. Revenue Revenue is measured at the transaction price that the Company receives or expects to receive as consideration for goods supplied and services rendered, net of returns and estimates of variable consideration such as discounts to customers. Revenue from the sale of goods includes Excise Duties and National Calamity Contingent Duty which are payable on manufacture of goods but excludes taxes such as VAT and Goods and Services Tax which are payable in respect of sale of goods and services. Revenue from the sale of goods and services is recognised when the Group performs its obligations to its customers and the amount of revenue can be measured reliably and recovery of the consideration is probable. The timing of such recognition in case of sale of goods is when the control over the same is transferred to the customer, which is mainly upon delivery and in case of services, in the period in which such services are rendered. Government Grant Group entities may receive government grants that require compliance with certain conditions related to the entity’s operating activities or are provided to the entity by way of financial assistance on the basis of certain qualifying criteria. Government grants are recognised when there is reasonable assurance that the grant will be received upon the Group entity complying with the conditions attached to the grant. Accordingly, government grants: (a) related to or used for assets, are deducted from the carrying amount of the asset. (b) related to incurring specific expenditures are taken to the Statement of Profit and Loss on the same basis and in the same periods as the expenditures incurred.
